title: Joe Turner’s Come and Gone starring Taraji P Henson and Cedric The En...
transcript: There's never a bad time to produce an August Wilson play, especially when you have a cast like this. Joe Turner's Come and Gone is the fourth of 10 plays in the Pittsburgh Cycle, taking place in 1911 at a boarding house in Pennsylvania. The main plot revolves around a mysterious guest named Herald who shows up to the boarding house with his daughter, looking for his wife. Long time husband and wife Seth and Bertha who own and run the boarding house have opposing feelings about him, but it becomes evident to everyone that he is deeply troubled. There are other characters at the boarding house throughout the play who each have their own little side plots. A lot of it didn't initially seem relevant to me, but I found that it all came together thematically in a really thoughtful way — I should have never doubted you, August Wilson. The other nice aspect of this is the ensemble work that this structure affords and the way it highlights a bunch of fantastic performances. Taraji P Henson and Cedric The Entertainer are wonderfully funny together, Ruben Santiago-Hudson gives a great portrayal of the free-spirited Bynum Walker, but it's Joshua Boone who steals the show as Herald Loomis, the man looking for his wife. He has a haunting energy that clouds the entire room whenever he's on stage — just an incredibly captivating presence that fuels an absolutely electrifying climax to both acts. I think he's got his Tony nomination in the bag. Overall, this was a great production of a somewhat understated but beautiful play about seeking identity, faith, and community in the wake of slavery. It's currently running on Broadway through July. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
